course_description:
This course covers theories and models relating to human development across the lifespan. It focuses on application of this knowledge to direct practice and examines the effects of diversity and adversity on children and adults throughout the lifespan.

SWSP1044 applies knowledge about human development to social work practice. The course aims to develop students’ understanding of the multidimensional nature of human development.

This course introduces issues concerning the nature of development across the lifespan, including

(a) understanding development in terms of change and stability,

(b) understanding the factors that influence development, and

(c) understanding major concepts and theories used in describing and explaining human development.

Social Work and Human Services are professions which are informed by a variety of theoretical frameworks that regard personalities, behaviours, choices and actions within the contexts in which they occur. Sound knowledge of human growth and development is a valuable tool for understanding people. It enables an appreciation, at once, of people’s potentials and capabilities, the challenges they may encounter, and the factors affecting their well-being over time. Much of social work and human services practice is about facilitating healthy growth and adjustment, overcoming constraints and increasing their options, and helping individuals respond to typical transitions, developmental tasks, and crises occurring throughout the lifespan. A sound knowledge of human growth and development can be a valuable tool in understanding people, their problems, and the contextual factors that may aid or hinder development and adaptation.

This course will provide the necessary foundational knowledge for students to understand the bio-psycho-social functioning and well-being of people. Students will begin to examine how they can usefully and appropriately apply knowledge about human development when communicating with others, making assessments and planning interventions in a variety of contexts. Throughout the course, knowledge will be linked directly to actual or potential practice issues.

Please be aware that this course examines challenges and risk factors that influence human development. As social workers, we work in areas that many people would find difficult, for example, in child protection; and with people trying to cope with trauma, loss, and bereavement. As such, this course will, at times, cover confronting content that may be challenging for some students or have the potential to cause distress. If you feel that you are upset by any of the content please feel free to contact me. Student services also provide counselling services . You are welcome to contact the Student Support and Wellbeing Services at 1300 275 870 or via email at student.services@uq.edu.au

learning_outcomes.description: Demonstrate knowledge of human development to inform social work practice.
Evaluate a range of theories of human development and the values and assumptions underpinning them.
Understand and evaluate the contextual factors that impact on human development across the lifespan.
Analyse, assess and develop a social work response to people’s experiences across the life course.

assessment_details.task_description: This description is only a summary of the task. For full details, including the marking rubric, please refer to the course Learn UQ (Blackboard) site. In this task, you will work in a small group (3-4 students) to analyse a case study and present your ideas as a professional conversation. You will: Analyse the case using concepts from human development Apply a range of theories from the course Discuss how the person can be supported Each group member will present a different theory and apply it to the case. The group will then engage in a shared discussion, comparing perspectives and proposing a supported response. Students will have 7.5 minutes per person (total of 22.5 minutes for a group of three, or 30 minutes for a group of 4) Presentations will be delivered in person in Week 10 (and may occur outside of scheduled tutorial times), and supported by PowerPoint Slides. Slides are due at the end of Week 9. This task assesses your ability to: Apply theory to practice Think critically about different perspectives Work collaboratively and communicate professionally Note : This task is designed to be challenging and authentic. You may use AI and/or machine translation (MT) tools; however, these provide limited support for the type of critical thinking required. You must clearly acknowledge any use of AI or MT tools. Failure to do so may constitute student misconduct under the Student Code of Conduct. To pass this assessment, you must demonstrate your own understanding of the content. You can request 1 discretionary extension for 48 hours for a single assessment task per semester, with no supporting evidence required. You can apply using the standard application form if:

Requests for extensions received after the assessment item submission due date may not be approved. Late requests must include evidence of the reasons for the late request as per the guidelines my.UQ .
The extension granted should be in proportion to the period of illness or disruption caused by the exceptional circumstances and will typically be no more than the specified maximum extension length for each assessment.
A maximum of three assessment requests can be submitted for each assessment, and the third request must include an Assessment Management Plan.
Students who have been ill or unable to attend class for more than 4 weeks in a semester are advised to carefully consider whether they are capable of successfully completing their courses and may need to consider applying for removal of course.

This will allow you to request extensions of up to 7 days (for first extension requests), without providing additional supporting documentation. This will not apply for assessments that do not allow extensions.
Student Access Plan: If you are experiencing a disability, chronic medical condition or other personal circumstances which impact your university studies, you should first register for support with Student Support and Wellbeing Services .
For SAP extensions longer than 7 calendar days, or subsequent extension requests for the same assessment task:

Outcome of Application
· Extension requests are generally processed within 2 working days.
Late submission
A penalty of 10% of the maximum possible mark will be deducted per 24 hours from time submission is due for up to 7 days. After 7 days, you will receive a mark of 0.

assessment_details.other_conditions: Time limited, Secure. See the conditions definitions
assessment_details.task_description: This final assessment task ( Exam - Quiz and Case Analysis ) is a closed-book assessment of 120 minutes (plus 10 minutes of reading time). It is an opportunity for you to demonstrate your knowledge and understanding of human development as a multidimensional process and to show how it may inform social work’s contribution to enhancing human wellbeing in line with “[p]rinciples of social justice, human rights, collective responsibility, and respect for diversity” (IFSW/IASSW 2014). To this end, your end-of-semester exam will be based on a case study , provided in Week 12, and require you to answer 20 multiple choice questions, a set of four short-answer questions and one short essay question which together will – Test your knowledge of relevant theories (and/or models and/or approaches) and concepts covered during this semester and your application of these theories (and/or models and/or approaches) and concepts to the case study provided, to analyse the specified character's current situation (that is, at the point of seeking social work support). Your analysis should take into consideration factors that have impacted the character's development through the stages of lifespan development covered in Weeks 8 to 13. This entails attention to the character's developmental tasks and transitions during these stages, highlighting both sources of risk, adversity, and resilience , as well as strengths and difficulties displayed. Based on the analysis conducted, propose interventions to support the main character in coping with past and current adversities, risks and difficulties, promote their strengths, and enhance their resilience. Additional Information Students are permitted to prepare and bring ONE (1) page of handwritten notes into the exam . This means: There cannot be anything written on the back of the page, and the notes must not be typed. The examination supervisor will check every student’s notes. Anyone, who has more than the one permitted page or whose notes are typed up (printed) rather than handwritten, will have their notes confiscated, and the matter will be treated as potential misconduct. Note : This assessment task must be completed in person. The use of generative Artificial Intelligence (AI) tools will not be permitted. Any attempted use of Generative AI may constitute student misconduct under the Student Code of Conduct. Read full task description Hide full task description

learning_activities.topic: Week 1 Lecture: Introduction - A Multidimension Approach to Lifespan Development This introductory lecture provides the foundation for the contents covered in the remainder of the semester. It comprises two parts: An overview of the course and its relevance to social work practice, including a discussion of the structure, content and assessment in the course. An introduction to Harms' (2021) multidimensional approach to human development as an overarching framework to locate, critique, and apply the theories and debates covered in this course. Reading: Harms (2021) Chapter 1

Week 2 Lecture: Development in Relational Contexts In this lecture, we continue to explore Harms' (2021) multidimensional approach, focusing on the relational and social dimensions of human development. Reading: Harms (2021) Chapter 2
Week 2 Tutorial: Development in Relational Contexts Review and exploration of lecture content and assessment preparation

Week 3 Lecture: Development in Structural and Cultural Contexts We continue to explore Harms' (2021) multidimensional approach, focusing on the structural and cultural dimensions of human development. Reading: Harms (2021) Chapter 3
Week 3 Tutorial In this tutorial we explore Harm's Multidimensional approach and apply it to a case study.
Week 4 Lecture: Assessment 1 (In-Class Quiz) In this lecture we complete the In-Class Quiz. Please ensure you arrive on time to the lecture.

Week 4 Tutorial: Development in Structural and Cultural Contexts Review and exploration of lecture content and assessment preparation. It is imperative to attend this tutorial as we will form groups for Assessment 2.

Week 5 Lecture: Pre-birth and Infancy This lecture explores the first stage of human development, the antenatal stage through to birth. We then examine development in infancy with an overview of physical, neurobiological, cognitive, social, emotional, and personality development. Our theory in focus this week is attachment theory. Reading: Harms (2021) Chapter 4
Week 5 Tutorial: Pre-birth and Infancy Review and exploration of lecture content and assessment preparation

Week 6 Lecture: Development in Early Childhood This lecture focuses on the developmental tasks and transitions in early childhood, as well as key sources of risk, adversity, and resilience during this stage of the lifespan. Our theory in focus is Piaget's theory of cognitive development. Reading: Harms (2021) Chapter 5
Week 6 Tutorial: Development in Early Childhood Review and exploration of lecture content and assessment preparation

Week 7 Lecture: Development in Middle Childhood This week, we examine the developmental tasks and transitions in middle childhood, as well as key sources of risk, adversity, and resilience during this stage of the lifespan. Theory in focus this week: Vygotsky's sociocultural theory of cognitive development. Reading: Harms (2021) Chapter 6
Week 7 Tutorial: Development in Middle Childhood Review and exploration of lecture content and assessment preparation

Week 8 Lecture: From Adolescence to Emerging Adulthood This week, we examine the developmental tasks and transitions in adolescence, as well as key sources of risk, adversity, and resilience during this stage of the lifespan. Theory in focus: Arnett's theory of emerging adulthood. We will consider this recently proposed stage of emerging adulthood - what does it entail, and how does it compare to adolescence? Readings: Harms (2021) Chapter 7; Arnett et al. (2019) Chapter 9
Week 8 Tutorial: From Adolescence to Emerging Adulthood Review and exploration of lecture content and assessment preparation

Week 9 Lecture: From Emerging to Young Adulthood We examine the developmental tasks and transitions in early adulthood, as well as key sources of risk, adversity, and resilience during this stage of the lifespan. We ask: How does it compare to the recently proposed stage of emerging adulthood? Reading : Harms (2021), Chapter 8; Arnett et al. (2019) Chapter 9
Week 9 Tutorial: Drop In Session for Assessment Support Assessment 2 and course check-in.
Mid-semester break

Week 10 Lecture: Development in Middle Adulthood This lecture explores the developmental tasks and transitions in middle adulthood, as well as key sources of risk, adversity, and resilience during this stage of the lifespan. Reading : Harms (2021) Chapter 9
Week 10 Tutorial: Assessment 2 - Group Presentations Please note group presentations may occur outside of regular scheduled tutorials.

Week 11 Lecture: Development in Late Adulthood This week, we focus on the developmental tasks and transitions in middle adulthood, as well as key sources of risk, adversity, and resilience during this stage of the lifespan. Reading: Harms (2021), Chapter 10
Week 11 Tutorial: Emerging to Young Adulthood, Development in MIddle Adulthood and Late Adulthood Review and exploration of lecture content and assessment preparation

Week 12 Lecture: Social Work at the End of Life While grief and loss are themes that pervade all social work practice, at the end of the semester, we want to consider the relevance of these themes for the end of life and for those left behind. Reading : Harms (2021) Chapters 11 & 12

Week 12 Tutorial: Assessment 3 - Case Study Analysis In this tutorial we will examine the case study and begin preparations for the End of Semester Exam. We will practice applying the case study to short answer questions.
Week 13 Lecture: Course Revision and Conclusion In preparation for your exams, we will review and revise the contents covered in this course.
Week 13 Tutorial: Course Revision and Conclusion This is tutorial we will continue to examine the case study and apply it to an example of a short essay question.
